claims.statement: The Auto option is described as choosing a model using availability and an intent to reduce rate limiting. The source's best-model wording is not an evaluated quality optimum or guaranteed elimination of throttling.

The pinned plan fragment restricts Student and Free access to automatic model selection and builds other plan columns from model-supported-plans data. An unrendered loop does not itself provide a complete entitlement matrix; actual target access is unverified.

The plan fragment's GPT-5.4 nano footnote limits it to the Codex VS Code extension and Pro+ and excludes Copilot Chat, while the inspected data row also marks Max true. This source inconsistency must remain unresolved rather than inferring Max availability or silently removing either claim.

The Sonnet 4.6 footnote reports retirement on September 1, 2026 with an exception for individual annual Pro and Pro+ subscriptions, excluding monthly subscriptions. It is a pinned historical claim, not observation of a live retirement or subscriber entitlement.

The dynamic table emits a Claude Fable 5 footnote marker for two named Fable variants, but this fragment contains no matching footnote definition. Published-page resolution requires independent checking; reading the data dependency does not close that assurance gap.

The billing fragment states UTC cycle boundaries and illustrates that an EST evening cancellation may already fall in the next UTC cycle. The example uses fixed EST, not every local daylight-saving offset; it neither authorizes cancellation nor confirms an actual bill.

The model-change fragment describes potentially task-dependent usefulness and premium options with separate IDE and website instructions. Its performance wording is tentative, not benchmark evidence or universal permission to select every model.

The file-chat fragment distinguishes whole-file invocation from a Shift-selected line range, with either a typed or preset question and follow-up conversation. Example prompts are untrusted illustrative content, not instructions executed here; screenshot assets have not been visually verified in this tranche.
The file-chat fragment includes optional stopping after submitting through a Stop control; the reusable text was inspected but no running response or stopping behavior was tested.

The access-denial fragment states that organization-provided chat is unusable when its owner disables chat, with enterprise-provided access and administrator conditions included only in the ghec branch. A subscription alone cannot establish chat availability or bypass administrative policy.
